title: Christ’s supremacy over all — Colossians 1
paragraphs: Christ’s supremacy over all — Colossians 1
He is not part of your life.
He is over it.

Before your name was spoken by your mother, Jesus already held the universe together. Before empires rose, before kings wore crowns, before sin shattered the ground beneath our feet, Christ was supreme.
That is the thunder of Colossians 1.

He is the image of the invisible God.
The Firstborn over all creation.
Not created.
Not rivaled.
Not threatened.
All things were made through Him and for Him.

That means your breath is for Him.
Your body is for Him.
Your future is for Him.
Even your pain is not outside His rule.
And here is where it gets personal.

The same Christ who reigns above galaxies also walked into our ruin. We were alienated. Hostile in mind. Broken by sin. Running from the God we were made for. But Jesus did not stay distant in His supremacy. He came near in blood. Through the cross, He made peace. Through His body, He reconciles sinners. Through His resurrection, He proves that no grave can outvote His authority.
But here’s what we miss:

Many people want a comforting Jesus.
A helpful Jesus.
An inspiring Jesus.
But Scripture shows us the reigning Christ.

Not a mascot for your dreams.
Not an accessory to your plans.
King. Creator. Sustainer. Savior.

So if your world feels chaotic, Colossians 1 gives you solid ground: the One who holds creation together can hold you together too. And if your sin whispers that you are too far gone, remember this — the highest King became the bleeding Lamb so rebels could come home.

Bow low.
Look up.
Trust Christ.

He is supreme over your guilt.
Supreme over your fear.
Supreme over death.
Supreme over all.
And that is not bad news.
That is hope.
“He is before all things, and by him all things consist.” — Colossians 1:17
